The Hour is among the names of the Day of Resurrection: it is called al-Sa'a (the Hour), al-Haqqa (the Inevitable), al-Sakhkha (the Deafening Blast), al-Waqi'a (the Event), al-Tamma (the Overwhelming Calamity), and others. Each of these descriptions contains an aspect of terror and fright.

We notice the connection between the end of Surat al-Najm and the beginning of Surat al-Qamar. There He said: ﴿The imminent one has drawn near﴾ [al-Najm: 57], and here He said: ﴿The Hour has drawn near, and the moon has split﴾ [al-Qamar: 1]. We have said that the mere sending of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is one of the signs of the Hour, and we know that the Hour will not come except upon the worst of creation, at a time when no one on earth says: "Allah, Allah."

As for the people of the graves, from the time of our master Adam (peace be upon him) until those who die before the Hour arrives, as we have said, time for them is suspended, because time is a consequence of events; when events do not exist, time does not exist.

Therefore the Exalted said about them: ﴿As if they had not remained but an evening or its morning﴾ [al-Nazi'at: 46], referring to the Resurrection ﴿on the day they see it﴾ [al-Nazi'at: 46]. The man who argued with Ibrahim about his Lord, Allah caused him to die for one hundred years, and after Allah revived him he said: ﴿I have remained a day or part of a day...﴾ [al-Baqara: 259].

The People of the Cave also said this after three hundred and nine years, because this is the period a sleeper may spend in his sleep. Likewise, the period of the barzakh (the intermediate state) will pass over the people of the graves in this manner, as if they had slept a sleep and then arose from it.

Allah, glorified and exalted, is the Owner of time; He is the One who withholds and extends (al-Qabid and al-Basit). He withholds it from whomever He wills and extends it for whomever He wills.

The meaning of ﴿The Hour has drawn near﴾ [al-Qamar: 1] is: it is near to you on the personal level. So do not look at the minor signs and then the major signs and say: "There is still a long time between us and the Resurrection." No, this is not how the concept of the Resurrection should be understood.

For the human being, the Resurrection is his death. It is not after thousands or millions of years, because the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Yes," since he has passed from the stage of this world to the stage of the Hereafter, and his deeds in this world have ceased. Allah, the Exalted, kept the time and place of death hidden so that a person remains mindful of it at every moment.

As for the words of the Exalted: ﴿And the moon has split﴾ [al-Qamar: 1], the splitting of the moon is a cosmic sign established by the Book and the Sunna. It is reported that the moon split for the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), until Mount Hira appeared between the two halves. People of that time who were able to see it did witness it in this form.

We do not say that the entire world saw it, because cosmic signs are miracles intended to affirm the messengers and demonstrate their truthfulness in conveying from Allah. It is not necessary that everyone of that era see this sign. How could it be otherwise, when today, despite immense scientific progress and the availability of communication means, we hear of an eclipse occurring at such-and-such a time, and the various channels broadcast it, yet despite the announcement of the phenomenon in advance, only a few are able to see it? The moon is a nighttime sign at a time when most people are asleep.

Furthermore, the miracles and cosmic signs of the messengers are not intended to be permanent miracles; rather, they are a miracle for those who witness them, so that the one who is a believer may remain steadfast in his faith, or the one who is a disbeliever may believe in Allah.

For this reason they said: it is like a match that works only once. Likewise are all the miracles of the messengers. Had the Qur'an not informed us of the staff of Musa, we would have known nothing about it.

These cosmic signs are a breach of the established laws at the moment they occur; then things return to their natural state. The moon did indeed split and broke the custom, then it returned to what it had been after the disbelievers of Makkah, who denied the Messenger of Allah, saw it. Not all the disbelievers, but some of them; the portion of them who witnessed the miracle is sufficient to establish it.

They said: the meaning of ﴿The Hour has drawn near﴾ [al-Qamar: 1] is: the hour of each person, the appointed term he awaits. And ﴿the moon has split﴾ [al-Qamar: 1] means: it is split off from him, disappears, and withdraws from his life.

Since Allah, the Exalted, said ﴿has drawn near﴾ [al-Qamar: 1], it has indeed drawn near, so do not investigate this matter.

The Exalted also said: ﴿The command of Allah has come, so do not seek to hasten it. Glorified is He and exalted above what they associate with Him﴾ [al-Nahl: 1]. He said "has come" in the past tense, as if it had already occurred. How then does He say ﴿so do not seek to hasten it﴾ [al-Nahl: 1]? They said: because it was Allah who said "has come," and no one can object to Him or prevent Him from fulfilling what He has announced.

Likewise in His words ﴿The Hour has drawn near﴾ [al-Qamar: 1]: it has indeed drawn near, either the hour of each person when his term comes, which is close, or the general Hour, which is also near, because the splitting of the moon is among its signs, and the sending of the Messenger (ﷺ) is among its signs.

It is related that the deniers of the Messenger said to him: "If you are truthful in what you report, then bring us a sign now that proves your truthfulness." They were: al-Walid ibn al-Mughira, Abu Jahl ibn Hisham, al-As ibn Wa'il, al-As ibn Rabi'a, al-Aswad ibn Abd Yaghuth, al-Aswad ibn Abd al-Muttalib, Rabi'a ibn al-Aswad, and al-Nadr ibn al-Harith.

All of these and others attended this event, when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) supplicated and asked his Lord, and the moon was split into two halves: one half over Mount Abu Qubais, and one half over Qaynuqa', until the cave of Hira appeared between them. When they saw that, they said: "This is magic." As for the people of reason, they said: "Let us ask the travellers in the desert far from this place." When they asked them, they said: "Yes, we saw it." Others said: "We did not see it."

Imam Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) attributed this disagreement to the fact that the sign of the splitting of the moon is a nighttime sign: some saw it indeed, while some, indeed most, did not see it.

By surveying the verses that describe the establishment of the Hour and the signs that precede it, we read: ﴿When the sun is wound up, and when the stars fall, they scatter﴾ [al-Takwir: 1-2], and much else that portrays for us the collapse of these entities.

As for the moon, the only mention is His words: ﴿When the sight is dazzled, and the moon is eclipsed﴾ [al-Qiyama: 7-8]. The eclipse is lighter and less than the winding up of the sun.

From this we understand that the event of the splitting of the moon in this world is being stored for it in the Hereafter, so it will not undergo what happens to other stars.

For this reason He, glorified, says: ﴿And the Horn will be blown, and whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth will swoon, except whom Allah wills...﴾ [al-Zumar: 68]. Thus there are those who will swoon and those who will be saved.

In the Messenger of Allah's (ﷺ) description of the scene of the Resurrection he says: "When I regained consciousness, I found my brother Musa holding onto the pillar of the Throne." This means that he (peace be upon him) was not among those who swooned, and for this the Messenger of Allah was amazed.

Then it was made clear that he had swooned once in this world, at Mount Sinai: ﴿When his Lord manifested Himself to the mountain, He made it crumble to dust, and Musa fell down in a swoon...﴾ [al-A'raf: 143]. Allah, glorified and exalted, would not have combined two swoonings upon His prophet Musa; so when he swooned in this world, He saved him from the swoon of the Hereafter.

This is the exception: ﴿except whom Allah wills...﴾ [al-Zumar: 68].

The same applies to the matter of the splitting of the moon. This means that the splitting was real, a cosmic sign that took the moon out of its nature and condition; therefore what happens to the other stars in the Hereafter will not befall it.

And they denied: that is, they denied the manifest signs. Denial is a statement that contradicts reality, and it is a blameworthy trait in the eyes of all people. These people denied out of obstinacy and by following their desires; they followed their own whims. So desire calls its owner to deny the truth in order to fulfil what he wishes, and desire does not call its owner to good; it calls him only to evil and ruin, as the Exalted said: ﴿And follows his desire, and whose affair is ever neglect﴾ [al-Kahf: 28]. And the Truthful, glorified is He, said about them: ﴿They follow nothing but assumption and what their souls desire...﴾ [al-Najm: 23]. So the desire of the soul dominates them and controls their conduct.

And every matter is settled: every matter, whether of disbelief or faith, obedience or disobedience, every matter of theirs is settled toward a known end and a term that Allah knows. And Allah's knowledge of things is eternal: before a thing happens, Allah knows it, and the recording scribes have written it down.

So when the Truthful, glorified is He, decreed the disbelief of the disbeliever, He did not compel him to disbelieve; rather He left him the choice. But by His eternal knowledge, He wrote down what would happen from him. This is from His greatness, exalted is He, and the all-encompassing nature of His knowledge, glorified is He, of what has been, what will be, and what would not have been...

This is the meaning of ﴿And every matter is settled﴾: yes, settled, in the knowledge of Allah. So do not weary yourself, O Muhammad, and do not exert yourself in calling these people; your duty is only to deliver the message. As for faith and disbelief, it has already been decided in Allah's knowledge that this one will believe and his settled place is Paradise, and this one will disbelieve and his settled place is the Fire.

So the desires of these deniers will not change this settled place at all, because it is fixed and recorded in the Preserved Tablet, the Mother of the Book, which no one can alter.

...so Allah, glory be to Him, did not wrong them, nor did He seize them unawares. Rather, He sent them warning in advance. And what a warning it was, after a call that continued for a thousand years less fifty, in which Nuh warned them of the punishment of Allah. As they say: he who warns has absolved himself (qad a'dhara man andhar).

The Qur'an was revealed to argue with the disbelievers of Makkah and to persuade them, so it gave them a choice between these three matters: "Are your people better than the disbelievers before you whom Allah destroyed? Or do you have an exemption and a covenant in the earlier Scriptures that Allah will not punish you? Or will your multitude and your numbers avail you?"

These three are answered with a negation. You have no superiority over those who came before you, and you have no exemption from the punishment, because Allah the Exalted has not granted exemption to anyone, and He has not permitted the denial of His messengers.
